data.name: Outreaches
data.headline: From $255 • Bring the critters to your classroom
data.description:
Interacting with animals is a fun and unique way for students to learn about the world around them. We offer a variety of programs that give kids in San Diego the chance to meet cute critters while learning lessons that complement their grade level’s NGSS and incorporate STEM. Year-round field trips to the Center or outreaches to your classroom are offered for preschool, elementary, middle and high school classes.

* If you are a school, please call us at 858-756-4117 ext 318 or email us at education@animalcenter.org to reserve your spot, this way we can book you without upfront payment, and then we will invoice you at the time of program completion to get an accurate and final headcount.
data.itinerary:
* The program will begin with a brief introduction and set up rules and expectations.
* Animal presentations are 15 minutes per species. Typically we introduce the individual animal then talk about its species based on the focus of the grade-level theme, allowing for interaction and questions near the end of the presentation.
* The STEM activity is 30 minutes and typically done at the end.
data.group_size: Maximum 3 classes for 60-minutes or 2 classes for 90-minutes in a day
data.what_is_included:
_All grade lesson_
* **“Remember Me Thursday®”**  – Discuss pet overpopulation and how we can make positive change for orphan pets by remembering pet adoption. We encourage your class to celebrate with Helen Woodward Animal Center’s Remember Me Thursday® event in September!
* Outreaches will meet a dog, rabbit, dove, and box turtle.


_Preschool & Elementary School lessons_
* **Preschool and Kindergarten:** “Plants and Paws” – Understand the needs of plants and animals and how they’re connected to each other and their environment.
* Outreaches will meet a dog, rabbit, dove, and leopard gecko.

* **1st Grade:** “The Wonderful World of Animals” – Discover the different ways animals interact with the world and why these interactions vary depending on the species. 
* Outreaches will meet a dove, guinea pig, bearded dragon, and Madagascar hissing cockroach.

* **2nd Grade:** “Home is Where the Heart Is” – Explore different habitats and discover the types of animals that live in each one. 
* Outreaches will meet a guinea pig, leopard gecko, parrot, and beetle.

* **3rd Grade:** “Learning about Life Cycles” – Investigate the many unique life cycles of animals and why it is appropriate for their environment. 
* Outreaches will meet a skink, frog, dog, and dove.

* **4th Grade:** “The Senses of Survival” – Dive into the animal world where our five senses have gone wild and learn how animals perceive the world. It can be similar to the way that we do, or it can be very different! 
* Outreaches will meet a snake, Madagascar hissing cockroach, rabbit, and parrot.

* **5th Grade:** “You Are What You Eat” – Explore the food web and how everything in our ecological community is connected. 
* Outreaches will meet a snake, rabbit, dove, and Madagascar hissing cockroach.


_Middle School lessons_
* **6th Grade:** “System Overload” – Understand the way that animals have adapted, or failed to adapt, to the environmental changes that humans have created with the growth of civilization. Discuss ways we can improve our energy usage and be more aware of our actions on the ecosystem. 
* Outreaches will meet a frog, dove, dog, and California desert tortoise.

* **7th Grade:** “We’re All in This Together” – Discuss some of the ways that people impact the world around them and what we can do to provide positive change. 
* Outreaches will meet a blue-tongued skink, Madagascar hissing cockroach, rabbit, and parrot.

* **8th Grade:** “Diversity by Design” – Classify animals into different groups based on their external characteristics and understand how this isn’t the only method. Plus, understand how even animals in different classifications can have similarities. 
* Outreaches will meet a parrot, beetle, frog and guinea pig.


_High School lessons_
* **9th – 12th Grades:** “Biodiversity and Beyond” – Analyze how organisms maintain life through diversity and how they adapt to their surroundings. 
* Outreaches will meet a frog, snake, parrot, and rabbit.

* **9th – 12th Grades:** “Wild at Work” – Most people think of veterinarians when they think about careers with critters, but there are so many options out there! Discover all the unique careers that allow you to work with animals! 
* Outreaches will meet a dog, guinea pig, parrot, and snake.
data.cancellation_notes:
- We operate rain or shine.
- Canceling 31+ days prior: Will result in a refund of 75% of the paid value.
- Canceling within 30 days of your scheduled event: Will result in no refund.
- Rescheduling 31+ days prior: Will result in a fee of 30% of the paid value.
- We will allow your program to be rescheduled without a penalty for up to 3 business days once it has been booked. We are not able to reschedule within 30 days of your scheduled event and you will not receive a refund.
data.booking_notes:
#We are looking forward to seeing you!
Education Outreaches include animal encounters and interactive educational activities that meet grade-level STEM and NGSS.
- If you chose the 60-minute version and did not select STEM as part of our time with you, we should leave paperwork copies for each teacher which explains the STEM activity we would have done and provides a template if applicable. If you did not receive this, please email us and we can send it electronically to you.
- *Some* of our STEM activities include follow-up activities for the class to complete after we leave, if the teacher so desires. We will leave paperwork copies for each teacher which explains the follow up activity and provides any applicable templates. If you did not receive this and believe you should have, please email us and we can send it electronically to you if applicable.
- - -
**CLASSROOM EXPECTATIONS**
- We will arrive ~15 minutes before the start time to check in, set up our equipment, and let the animals get used to their surroundings. It is very helpful if we can set up before the children are present.
- Please inform us before the visit where we should park if there are special instructions. It is easier to unload our vehicle if we can park close to the building. We can move our vehicle after we unload if necessary.
- An indoor area where the students can sit comfortably in a half circle so everyone can easily see is required. If an outdoors location is the only option, it limits our animals to only reptiles and invertebrates for animal safety purposes.
- Remaining in the same location throughout the visit and having each class come to us is necessary. This reduces stress on the animals and helps us stay on time as we bring many supplies with us that are difficult to keep packing/unpacking between classes.
- In order to best serve the students and maintain animal health and safety, we only present to one class at a time (20-30 students maximum). 
- Our staff are trained on positive classroom management strategies, but we appreciate continued support from the teacher to ensure the best experience for the children and the animals.
data.check_in_details: We will check in at the office and head to the designated room to await your class' arrival.
data.pricing:
* $255 per class for 60-minute
* $315 per class for 90-minute
* Schools: we will invoice you after the program has finished so we can get a final headcount.

* Ask if you qualify for our grant-funded outreaches! If 60% or more of your students are eligible for free reduced price meals, you likely qualify.
data.special_requirements: * Must be at least 5-years old to pet reptiles.
data.restrictions:
* Indoors is best in order for us to safely present our animals. Outdoors can be done if there's no indoor option, but it will restrict the species we can bring to mainly reptiles and invertebrates.
* Minimal movement for our animals is best, so setting up in one space and having classes come to us is ideal for animal health and safety.
* We operate on a per class basis and do not provide experiences as an assembly-style with numerous classes. In order to get the full effect of our animals and to be able to provide interactions, the presentations per class are necessary.
* We can only do 1 curriculum per day, so if you are planning for us to visit multiple grade levels in 1 day, you'll need to select the curriculum that will work best for all of them.
* Outreaches only available for schools. We do not visit people's residences.
